text:
maria-cs: Hey team, customer reported duplicate partial outputs + double billing after an SSE reconnect. They say it happens right after an auth token refresh from their SDK.

maria-cs: Short repro they gave: 1) Start streaming generation via SSE with token A. 2) Client gets token refresh -> token B. 3) Connection blips, client reconnects using token B and sends resume_token. 4) Server resumes and emits a short partial chunk that the client already received just before disconnect, then continues — customer got billed for the duplicate chunk.

dave-support: Can you paste the minimal logs they provided? any request ids / session ids?

maria-cs: Copied log snippets from customer (redacted):
```
[2026-02-11T14:22:10Z] SSE open session_id=ss-9f2a, auth=Bearer A
[2026-02-11T14:22:34Z] DEBUG: sending chunk seq=45 session=ss-9f2a
[2026-02-11T14:22:35Z] WARN: auth token rotated -> new token B
[2026-02-11T14:22:36Z] ERROR: connection dropped (network)
[2026-02-11T14:22:36Z] reconnect attempt using auth=Bearer B resume_token=rt-332
[2026-02-11T14:22:36Z] INFO: server resumed session? resumed_seq=45 emitted_seq=45 session=ss-9f2a
```

maria-cs: They highlighted that `emitted_seq=45` appears again immediately after reconnect.

ellen-sre: Hmm. Looks like the server accepted the resume_token even though auth changed. If session binding is tied to the auth token (or a token-derived session fingerprint) we could end up thinking it's the same session while the client already got the last chunk.

ivan-runtime: Do we have any codepaths where resume acceptance checks only resume_token validity and not whether the auth context equals the original session context? I thought we enforced `session_owner` check on resume.

ellen-sre: Currently we check `resume_token` -> map to `session_id` -> allow resume if `resume_token` not expired. We do a mild owner check but it uses a short-lived `auth_fingerprint` that is recomputed on token issuance. If the customer rotates tokens, the fingerprint changes and our check might either reject (which we haven't seen) or — due to a race — accept and re-emit the last in-flight chunk.

ops-bot: Alert: stream-reconnect spike @ 2026-02-11T14:22:36Z (5 failures across us-east-1). All traces with cause=NORMAL_CLOSE + auth_rotate=true.

dave-support: Customer wants reprieve for the duplicated charge. Can we reproduce? maria-cs, can you share their minimal client flow or a curl example?

maria-cs: They sent a tiny repro in node but here's an equivalent curl-ish flow:
```
# initial stream
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer A" -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=rw-3 \
  -d '{"prompt":"x"}\\n' \
  # receive up to seq=45
# token refresh happens externally -> now use B
# reconnect
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer B" -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?resume_token=rt-332&session_id=ss-9f2a"
```

ivan-runtime: I can repro locally by forcing a token rotate while a chunk is in-flight. Repro steps: open SSE, wait for chunk boundary, rotate token via refresh endpoint, drop connection, reconnect with resume_token. I see duplicate of last chunk ~90% of runs.

ivan-runtime: Root cause I think: when a chunk is mid-emit at disconnect, the acknowledgement/last_sent pointer isn't atomically checkpointed before the socket torn down. On resume we select `start_seq = last_sent` instead of `last_ack`, so the client sometimes gets the last_sent chunk again. Token rotation just increases chance because of timing jitter.

ellen-sre: That matches. Two fixes: short-term mitigation is to make resume start from `last_ack` (what client acked) instead of `last_sent` until we have a stronger idempotency layer. Longer-term: persist a durable checkpoint (server-side) at chunk boundaries and ensure resume only emits seq > last_ack.

dave-support: Possible customer mitigation while we fix?

ivan-runtime: Quick config toggle we can enable per-customer: `resume_prefer_last_ack=true` which will bias resume to advance beyond the last acknowledged sequence stored in the session metadata. Not perfect if client acking is lost, but reduces duplicates.

ellen-sre: Also consider an emergency rule: if `auth_fingerprint` changed within X seconds of disconnect, treat resume as potentially untrusted and require explicit `resume_flow=confirm` from client (SDK will retry full restart). That avoids silent duplicates at the cost of re-generation.

qa-bot: Add automated tests: (1) simulated token rotate at chunk boundary, assert no duplicate sequences; (2) stress test 1000 reconnects to measure duplicate rate. I can queue these once we have a patch.

maria-cs: Customer asked about credits. finance + support guidance? dave-support: we'll offer pro-rated credit for duplicated token charges immediately and follow up when patch lands.

ivan-runtime: I'll open an engineering ticket with steps and include a short patch to prefer `last_ack` on resume and add better atomics around checkpointing. Linking ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/RW-9876 (internal).

dave-support: Thanks. Action items: 1) ivan -> provisional config flip for this customer and patch PR, 2) ellen -> ops monitor + correlate auth_rotate spikes, 3) qa-bot -> add tests, 4) maria-cs -> send credit note draft to the customer and collect full request IDs.

maria-cs: I'll send credit and the repro to you all. ping me when PR is up and I'll ask customer to validate. :thumbsup:
